# PR #11 dependency hardening

Contribution: https://github.com/SpookySandwich/dsh-plugin-message-edit/pull/11
by anupamme (Anupam Mediratta), with an automated OrbisAI suggestion.
Reviewed contributor commit: `6893d486ecfcf2d354a31e95aca77a0b0f48879d`.
Integrated master: `2a2057b391218b7981014c10f1f302463d2d477a` (1.4.0).

## Advisory and selected version

[GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)
and the [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-104850)
identify MCP client versions `>=2.0.0 <2.2.0` as affected by OAuth credential
disclosure to an authorization server chosen by an untrusted MCP server.
Client 2.2.0 is the first 2.x release patched for this OAuth advisory only.
[GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw)
/ CVE-2026-111769, published October 20, affects client `>=2.0.0 <2.3.0`:
HTTP transports follow cross-origin redirects and resend custom headers;
307/308 redirects also forward request bodies. Client 2.3.0 fixes this
second advisory. The PR title/body say 2.2.0, but its actual diff selects
2.3.0 for both client and core, addressing both advisories. Retain that
contribution: npm registry metadata confirms both 2.3.0 versions, tarball
integrities, Apache-2.0 licenses, and the client's exact core dependency.

## Dependency scope

The checkout lockfile auto-installs the DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 peer host, which depends
on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.0-rc.2`, which pins MCP client 2.0.0.
An override is needed to change that exact transitive pin while retaining the
older host for compatibility testing. Keep the contributor's unversioned
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` override: official DSH 0.2.1-rc.2's bridge pins
client 2.2.0, which fixes the OAuth advisory but is still affected by the
redirect advisory. Narrowing to the older bridge would leave that newer
checkout host affected if selected. Review this pin when updating hosts.

No direct client/core dependency is needed: plugin sources do not import
either package, and the client supplies its matching core transitively.
Both inspected official bridges construct the HTTP transport with
`requestInit.headers`, without `authProvider`; they also support stdio.
No affected OAuth call path was found in this plugin or those bridge entry
points. However, their header-carrying HTTP transport is within the redirect
advisory's affected usage, without requiring OAuth. Exposure requires a
redirect to another origin; no real user's server or credentials were tested.
This is dependency hardening of the checkout host.

Client 2.3.0 intentionally follows redirects only within the same origin
on Node, and refuses redirects in browsers. Configure a server's final URL
when it relies on cross-origin redirects. `redirectPolicy: 'follow'` restores
the old exposure; this change does not enable it. Stdio is unaffected.

The override affects installs with this repository as the npm root. npm
ignores dependency packages' overrides, and the published plugin archive
does not bundle DSH or MCP packages or ship this lockfile. Installing this
plugin therefore does not patch an existing user's host. Host owners must
manage host dependency updates independently. The advisory also describes
issuer binding and stored-credential requirements for OAuth users; a package
version alone does not establish that every affected application is fixed.

## Local checks

Windows / Node 22.19.0 / npm 10.9.3:

- `npm ci`: passes after integrating master and restoring the broad override.
- `npm run build` and `npm test`: pass; 56 tests, zero failures or skips.
- `npm run check:release-tools`: passes all 4 tests.
- `npm run check:package` and `npm pack`: pass; 13 archive files, with no
  bundled dependencies or lockfile.
- `npm ls @modelcontextprotocol/client @modelcontextprotocol/core @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client --all`:
  passes; the older bridge resolves client/core 2.3.0.
- Round 2 local transport check uses the actual SDK and two loopback origins
  with synthetic `X-API-Key` and JSON notification data. All 8 cases pass:
  307/308 same-origin redirects retain header/body on both 2.2.0 and 2.3.0;
  cross-origin redirects leak both on 2.2.0 and are refused on 2.3.0 with
  zero requests to the other origin. The reproducible script and log are
  `round2-redirect-check.mjs` and `round2-redirect.log` in the event run folder.
  This directly tests the transport configuration shape used by DSH, without
  loading the bridge or claiming full MCP/OAuth interoperability.
- `npm audit --json`: the reviewed advisory is absent. There are 13 other
  findings (9 moderate, 4 high); this change is not a clean-audit claim.
- `node scripts/run-dsh-acceptance.mjs`: passes fresh boot and restart against
  isolated official DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 (client 2.0.0), official 0.2.1-rc.2
  (client 2.2.0), and the checkout's older host with overridden client 2.3.0.
  All three runs cover live/cold edits, images, offline model replies, source
  preservation, tree ancestry, sibling retry, nested branches and persisted
  seeded-branch recovery. These are plugin acceptance checks, not OAuth
  exploit or full MCP interoperability tests. The fixture does not load the
  MCP bridge, and separate official-runtime installs do not apply this
  repository's override.
  Round 2 repeats fresh/restart acceptance on the overridden checkout host;
  both phases pass after restoring the broad override.

The read-only `npm run check:release -- 1.4.0` reports npm HTTP 404. The
existing source version is not verified as an available npm release. This
pre-existing publication gap is outside this change.

## Release scope (`1.4.1`)

Prepared as patch release `1.4.1` (`v1.4.1`) with `Co-authored-by: anupamme <mediratta@gmail.com>` and candid checkout-only release notes:
- This change has no consumer runtime behavior change: the packed manifest's
  `overrides` entry is ignored by npm when `dsh-plugin-message-edit` is installed
  as a dependency, and `package-lock.json` does not ship in the published archive.
- Installing or updating this plugin does not patch or upgrade `@modelcontextprotocol/client`
  in an existing user's DSH host installation; host dependencies remain managed
  by the host environment.
- Manual npm publication is pending for `dsh-plugin-message-edit@1.4.1` (and `1.4.0`).
